subject: Embeddings vector profile, auth & batching — post-call recap
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Morgan <leah@heliocommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Embeddings vector profile, auth & batching — post-call recap

Thanks again for the call earlier, Leah — good conversation and clear production use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of what we heard (from Helio):
- Primary goal: migrate existing customer-product vectors into a fast semantic search + reranker flow for product discovery across web + mobile.
- Current vendor: VectorCloud (bulk export available).~1.2M vectors, ~512 dims, not L2-normalized.
- Target latency (search end-to-end): ~<120ms for top-K nearest neighbor + reranker, embedding-only QPS target ~200.
- Data residency: US-only; PCI not in scope but PII redaction required for descriptions.

Open/clarify items we requested on the call:
- Confirm the exact dimensionality and whether your export includes any per-vector metadata (doc_id, created_at, source).
- Sample export (CSV or parquet) shared to evaluate normalization and sparsity.
- Expected steady-state QPS and peak (you mentioned 200 steady / 500 burst).

Proposed technical scope for a pilot (high level):
1) Ingest sample export (10k-50k) into Redwood test workspace to validate embeddings compatibility (dimension, dtype).
2) Evaluate similarity metric (cosine vs dot) and recommend normalization approach.
3) Decide migration approach: keep existing vectors + build ANN index, or re-embed with recommended model (we'll provide cost/quality tradeoffs).
4) Integrate reranker path (cross-encoder) as optional second-pass; measure end-to-end latency.
5) Provide SDK/auth guidance, routing policy for hosted vs private, and a brief ops checklist for rollout.

Next steps (asks from Helio):
- Please share a small sample export (10k) and the QPS report you mentioned.
- Confirm one or two 30–45m slots next week for Marissa (SE) to review the sample and run a short architecture sync.

We'll prepare a short migration checklist and a pilot pricing note. If nothing else, I propose the following time for the SE pairing session: May 13, 10:00am PT. Let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priyom — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming a few items and attaching the sample export you asked for.

Quick answers:
- Export specifics: 1.2M total, primary vectors are 512 dimensions, CSV with columns: doc_id, vector_0..vector_511, title, created_at. We haven’t normalized — values are raw floats (VectorCloud format).
- QPS: typical steady-state for search embedding queries is ~180 qps globally; expected peak bursts up to ~450.
- Use-case: front-line product search (autocomplete + full-page results) with an eventual cross-encoder rerank for top 100.
- Security: US-only. We can provide an S3 presigned sample link or drop CSV via vendor-share.

Attached: heliocommerce_embeddings_metadata.csv (10k sample) and a short qps snapshot (heliocommerce_qps_report.pdf).

One question we have on migration: do you recommend re-embedding everything with Redwood-recommended model to standardize vectors, or can we take your suggestion to keep existing vectors in an ANN index and only re-embed high-traffic items? Cost/quality tradeoff guidance would help.

Leah Morgan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Morgan <leah@heliocommerce.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings vector profile, auth & batching — post-call recap

Hi Leah — thanks for the sample and the QPS snapshot. I reviewed the CSV quickly; attached notes are brief recommendations to get a pilot humming.

Short answers to your migration question: both approaches are valid; tradeoffs below.

Recommendation summary (pilot-first, iterative):
- Step 0: Validate sample vectors (done) — they look consistently 512 dims with no obvious zero-padding.
- Step 1: Index-first pilot: ingest existing vectors into an ANN index (HNSW) without re-embedding. This is lowest-cost and fastest to validate retrieval quality. Normalize on ingest (L2 -> unit vectors) for cosine similarity if you plan to use cosine; if you prefer dot-product, leave as-is but ensure consistent metric across query and index.
- Step 2: Evaluate quality delta by re-embedding a 10k subset with Redwood-recommended model (we'll run both and run an A/B on retrieval + reranker effectiveness). If re-embedding improves recall / reranker lift materially, we can schedule a staged re-embed.
- Step 3: Production migration pattern: hybrid approach — keep legacy vectors in cold store + ANN index, re-embed hot items on access, and schedule backfill for top N during low-traffic windows.

Technical details and ops knobs:
- Dimensions: support for 512 is native. If you re-embed to 768 later, the index must be rebuilt; plan for that cost. We can also project 768->512 with a learnable projection but recommend re-embedding for best quality.
- Normalization: we strongly prefer L2-normalized vectors for cosine similarity. For dot-product, no norm. We'll provide a one-line script to L2 normalize on ingest.
- Batching: for migration re-embed jobs, we recommend batch sizes of 64–256 depending on model and GPU type; for hosted realtime embedding requests, dynamic batching up to 32 is typical to keep latency <50ms per request under your QPS.
- Indexing: HNSW parameters: M=64, efConstruction=200, efSearch=100 (we can tune). For 1.2M vectors we recommend sharded HNSW across 4 shards initially.
- Reranker: run cross-encoder on top-100 candidates. We estimate reranker adds ~60–80ms depending on model; measure in pilot. Consider a lightweight filter (keyword boost) before rerank to reduce calls.

Auth / SDK / routing notes:
- SDK: use Redwood JS/Java client. Example call is a single POST with Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>. For Private deployments we'll provide ephemeral tokens + KMS integration options.
- Routing: easiest path is to pin search to the hosted model for embeddings, with a fallback to a cheaper model for degraded capacity. We'll document policy JSON for automatic fallback.
- Structured output / tool calling: not required for embeddings phase; keep separate for later catalog enrichment.

Pilot checklist (short):
- [Helio] Confirm S3 sample link or I/O mechanism for 10k sample (received).
- [Redwood] Run ingestion + L2 normalization on sample and return precision/recall vs current vendor index.
- [Joint] Define quality metric (Recall@10, MRR) and target improvement for re-embed decision.
- [Helio] Approve pilot window and data residency constraints.

I'll kick off the sample ingestion tomorrow morning and share the first retrieval snapshots by EOD. If you can confirm the May 13 SE pairing (10:00am PT) we will invite an infra engineer to discuss sharding and autoscaling.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
